source.title: Indian Polity (question set written from its topics)

chapter.name: Citizenship
chapter.blurb: The meaning of citizenship, constitutional provisions, the Citizenship Act 1955, and overseas citizenship of India.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes 'enemy aliens' as distinguished from 'friendly aliens' under Indian law?
questions.a: They are subjects of a country at war with India and enjoy lesser rights than friendly aliens
o: They are subjects of a country at war with India and enjoy lesser rights than friendly aliens
They are subjects of a country with which India has no diplomatic relations and they enjoy the same rights as friendly aliens
They are Indian citizens who have helped a hostile state and so lose their civil rights
They are subjects of any neighbouring country and are denied only the right to vote
questions.e: Enemy aliens are the subjects of the country that is at war with India and they enjoy lesser rights than friendly aliens.
w: Enemy status turns on a state of war, not on the absence of diplomatic ties, and enemy aliens enjoy fewer rights than friendly aliens.
Enemy aliens are by definition aliens, i.e. citizens of another state, not Indian citizens.
Neighbourhood is irrelevant; the test is war with India, and the rights denied are wider than the vote.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about eligibility for the office of President is correct, as compared with the USA?
questions.a: In India both citizens by birth and naturalised citizens are eligible, whereas in the USA only a citizen by birth is eligible
o: In India both citizens by birth and naturalised citizens are eligible, whereas in the USA only a citizen by birth is eligible
In India only a citizen by birth is eligible, whereas in the USA a naturalised citizen is also eligible
In both India and the USA only a citizen by birth is eligible
In India a naturalised citizen is eligible only after the Parliament approves, whereas in the USA no citizen is eligible without such approval
questions.e: In India both citizens by birth and naturalised citizens are eligible for President; in the USA only a citizen by birth.
w: This reverses the comparison: India admits naturalised citizens, whereas the USA requires a natural-born citizen.
India does not restrict the office to citizens by birth (Article 58 requires only that the person be a citizen of India), unlike the USA.
No parliamentary approval is needed; a naturalised citizen is eligible in India like any other citizen.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a right that friendly aliens enjoy but enemy aliens lack?
o: Equality of opportunity in the matter of public employment (Article 16)
questions.e: Enemy aliens do not enjoy protection against arrest and detention (Article 22); Articles 16, 19, 29-30 are citizen-only rights, so no alien holds them.
w: Equality of opportunity in public employment (Article 16) is a citizen-only right, denied to aliens of both kinds, so it does not separate enemy from friendly aliens.
Article 19 freedoms are conferred on citizens and denied to aliens of both kinds.
Articles 29 and 30 are citizen rights denied to aliens of both kinds.

questions.q: A trader from a country that has cordial relations with India has settled in an Indian city and wishes to form an association and practise his profession freely. Which of the following is correct?
questions.a: The freedoms of association and profession under Article 19 are conferred on citizens and denied to aliens, including friendly aliens
o: The freedoms of association and profession under Article 19 are conferred on citizens and denied to aliens, including friendly aliens
Article 19 freedoms extend to him because friendly aliens enjoy all the civil rights that citizens enjoy
He is denied Article 19 freedoms only if his country becomes an enemy of India
He enjoys Article 19 freedoms but not the right to vote, because the vote is the only right reserved for citizens
questions.e: Article 19 freedoms (speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession) are conferred on citizens and denied to aliens.
w: Aliens, friendly or enemy, do not enjoy all civil and political rights, and Article 19 is among the citizen-only rights.
Article 19 is denied to aliens as a class; enemy status only widens the loss (Article 22).
The vote is one of several citizen-only rights; Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30 are also reserved.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a duty that citizens owe to the Indian State?
questions.a: Paying taxes, respecting the national flag and national anthem and defending the country
o: Paying taxes, respecting the national flag and national anthem and defending the country
Voting in every election to the Lok Sabha and the state assembly
Compulsory military service for a fixed number of years
Surrendering all foreign property to the Union Government
questions.e: Citizens owe duties such as paying taxes, respecting the national flag and national anthem, and defending the country.
w: Voting is a legal right of citizens and is not a constitutional duty; voting is not compulsory.
No fixed period of compulsory military service is imposed; defending the country is a general duty (Article 51A(d)).
The Constitution and the law impose no duty to surrender foreign property.

questions.q:
With reference to aliens in India, consider the following statements:

1. Aliens are denied the political rights of citizens but enjoy all the civil rights.
2. Aliens are of two categories, namely friendly aliens and enemy aliens.
3. India has two kinds of people, namely citizens and aliens.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: aliens do not enjoy all the civil and political rights; Articles 15, 16 and 19 are civil rights confined to citizens. Statement 2 is correct: aliens are either friendly aliens or enemy aliens. Statement 3 is correct: the people of India are either citizens or aliens. So only 2 and 3 are correct.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: people in India are either citizens or aliens.
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: people in India are either citizens or aliens.
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: aliens are either friendly or enemy aliens.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rights the Constitution confers on citizens and denies to aliens:

1. The freedoms of movement, residence and profession are part of Article 19.
2. Protection against discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth is given by Article 15.
3. Cultural and educational rights are guaranteed by Articles 25 and 26.
4. Equality of opportunity in public employment is guaranteed by Article 16.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the freedoms of movement, residence and profession are part of Article 19. Statement 2 is correct: Article 15 protects against discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. Statement 3 is incorrect: cultural and educational rights are in Articles 29 and 30, while Articles 25 and 26 deal with religious freedom. Statement 4 is correct: Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment. So only 1, 2 and 4 are correct.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: Article 19 contains these freedoms.
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: Article 15 gives this protection.
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: Article 19 contains these freedoms.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rights and privileges of citizens of India:

1. A citizen by naturalisation is eligible for the office of President of India.
2. Citizens are eligible for the office of Governor of a state.
3. The right to contest for membership of Parliament and of the state legislature is conferred on citizens and denied to aliens.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: unlike the USA, India does not require the President to be a natural-born citizen, so a naturalised citizen is eligible. Statement 2 is correct: the office of Governor of a state is open to citizens and denied to aliens. Statement 3 is correct: the right to contest for Parliament and the state legislature belongs to citizens only. So all three are correct.
w: '1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: only citizens may contest for Parliament and state legislatures.
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: the Governor's office is open to citizens, not aliens.
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: India does not confine the Presidency to natural-born citizens.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding offices and political rights:

1. The right to vote in elections to the Lok Sabha and state legislative assembly extends to friendly aliens who have long resided in India.
2. Judges of the Supreme Court must be citizens, but judges of the high courts may be friendly aliens.
3. The Attorney General of India and the advocate general of a state are offices for which the Constitution makes citizens eligible and denies the same to aliens.
4. The offices of President and Vice-President are open to citizens and also to friendly aliens.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the right to vote is conferred on citizens and denied to aliens. Statement 2 is incorrect: judges of both the Supreme Court and the high courts must be citizens. Statement 3 is correct: the offices of Attorney General of India and advocate general of a state are open to citizens and denied to aliens. Statement 4 is incorrect: the offices of President and Vice-President are open only to citizens. So only 3 is correct.
w: '4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: these offices are open to citizens and denied to aliens.
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: the offices of President and Vice-President are confined to citizens.
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: these offices are open to citizens and denied to aliens.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Citizens owe allegiance both to the Union and to the state in which they live.
2. Friendly aliens enjoy the same rights as citizens, except the right to hold constitutional offices.
3. Citizens owe duties to the Indian State, for example paying taxes and defending the country.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: citizens owe allegiance only to the Union; there is no separate state citizenship. Statement 2 is incorrect: aliens do not enjoy all civil and political rights; the denied list goes beyond offices (Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, 30 and the vote). Statement 3 is correct: citizens owe duties to the Indian State, for example paying taxes and defending the country. So only 3 is correct.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: citizens owe duties such as paying taxes and defending the country.
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: aliens are denied rights beyond constitutional offices, including Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, 30 and the vote.
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: citizens owe duties such as paying taxes and defending the country.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Citizens are full members of the Indian State and owe allegiance to it.
2. Friendly aliens enjoy the right to vote in elections to the Lok Sabha because their countries have cordial relations with India.
3. Cultural and educational rights under Articles 29 and 30 are enjoyed by aliens and citizens alike.
4. Aliens are citizens of some other state and hence do not enjoy all the civil and political rights.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: citizens are full members of the Indian State and owe allegiance to it. Statement 2 is incorrect: the right to vote is reserved for citizens, whatever the relations of the alien's country with India. Statement 3 is incorrect: the cultural and educational rights of Articles 29 and 30 are among the rights denied to aliens. Statement 4 is correct: aliens are citizens of some other state and hence do not enjoy all the civil and political rights. So only 1 and 4 are correct.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: aliens belong to another state and so lack some civil and political rights.
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: the vote is reserved for citizens.
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: aliens belong to another state and so lack some civil and political rights.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Citizens are full members of the Indian State and enjoy all civil and political rights.
2. Respecting the national flag and the national anthem is a duty that citizens owe to the Indian State.
3. Aliens are persons who owe allegiance to the Indian State but are denied the vote.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: citizens are full members of the Indian State and enjoy all civil and political rights. Statement 2 is correct: respecting the national flag and the national anthem is a duty citizens owe to the Indian State. Statement 3 is incorrect: aliens are citizens of some other state; it is citizens who owe allegiance to the Indian State. So only 1 and 2 are correct.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: citizens enjoy all civil and political rights.
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: aliens do not owe allegiance to India; citizens do.
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: citizens enjoy all civil and political rights.

questions.q:
With reference to citizens and aliens, consider the following statements:

1. Equality of opportunity in public employment is conferred by Article 16 on aliens whose countries have cordial relations with India.
2. The office of Vice-President of India is open to citizens and denied to aliens.
3. The freedom of speech and expression under Article 19 is available to friendly aliens as it is to citizens.
4. Enemy aliens, unlike friendly aliens, lack protection against arrest and detention.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 16 is a citizen-only right. Statement 2 is correct: the offices of President and Vice-President are open to citizens and denied to aliens. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 19 freedoms are conferred on citizens and denied to aliens. Statement 4 is correct: Article 22 protection against arrest and detention is available to friendly aliens but not to enemy aliens. So only 2 and 4 are correct.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: Article 22 protection is denied to enemy aliens.
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: Article 22 protection is denied to enemy aliens.
'4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: these offices are open to citizens only.

questions.q:
With reference to the status of aliens, consider the following statements:

1. A person who is the subject of a country at war with India is an enemy alien.
2. Friendly aliens are eligible for the office of Governor of a state.
3. A friendly alien is eligible for the office of Attorney General of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: an enemy alien is the subject of a country at war with India. Statement 2 is incorrect: the office of Governor of a state is open to citizens and denied to aliens. Statement 3 is incorrect: the office of Attorney General of India is open to citizens, with the privilege denied to aliens. So only 1 is correct.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: an enemy alien is a subject of a country at war with India.
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: the Attorney General must be a citizen.
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: the Governor's office is confined to citizens.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about aliens:

1. A friendly alien is an Indian citizen who lives in a country with cordial relations with India.
2. Enemy aliens enjoy the same rights as friendly aliens apart from the right to vote.
3. Friendly aliens are the subjects of countries that have cordial relations with India.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: aliens are citizens of some other state, not Indian citizens. Statement 2 is incorrect: enemy aliens enjoy lesser rights than friendly aliens; for example, they have no Article 22 protection. Statement 3 is correct: friendly aliens are the subjects of countries that have cordial relations with India. So only one statement is correct.
w: Miscount: the correct statements are 3, which is only one, not none.
Miscount: the correct statements are 3, which is only one, not only two.
Miscount: the correct statements are 3, which is only one, not all three.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about aliens and citizens:

1. Enemy aliens are the subjects of a country with which India has cordial relations.
2. Protection against arrest and detention under Article 22 is denied to friendly aliens but available to enemy aliens.
3. Protection against discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth under Article 15 is enjoyed by aliens as it is by citizens.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: cordial relations mark friendly aliens; enemy aliens belong to a country at war with India. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is enemy aliens who lack Article 22 protection. Statement 3 is incorrect: protection under Article 15 is conferred on citizens and denied to aliens. So none is correct.
w: Miscount: the correct statements are none of them, which is none, not only one.
Miscount: the correct statements are none of them, which is none, not only two.
Miscount: the correct statements are none of them, which is none, not all three.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Attorney General of India is not among the offices reserved for citizens, which are limited to constitutional heads such as President and Governor.
2. In the USA both citizens by birth and naturalised citizens are eligible for the office of President.
3. Judges of the Supreme Court and the high courts are among the offices for which citizens are eligible and aliens are not.
4. The right to contest for Parliament and the state legislature is a right of citizens only.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the offices reserved for citizens include the Attorney General of India and the advocate general of states. Statement 2 is incorrect: in the USA only a citizen by birth is eligible for the office of President. Statement 3 is correct: judges of the Supreme Court and the high courts must be citizens. Statement 4 is correct: the right to contest for Parliament and the state legislature is a right of citizens only. So only two statements are correct.
w: Miscount: the correct statements are 3, 4, which is only two, not only one.
Miscount: the correct statements are 3, 4, which is only two, not none.
Miscount: the correct statements are 3, 4, which is only two, not all four.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Aliens do not enjoy all the civil and political rights of citizens.
Statement-II: Aliens are citizens of some other state.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: aliens do not enjoy all the civil and political rights of citizens. Statement-II is correct: aliens are citizens of some other state, and hence do not enjoy all the civil and political rights, so II is the reason for I.
w: Statement-II does give the reason: aliens belong to another state and hence lack some civil and political rights, so II is the reason for I.
Statement-II is actually correct: aliens are citizens of some other state.
Statement-I is actually correct: aliens do not enjoy all civil and political rights.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Enemy aliens enjoy lesser rights than friendly aliens.
Statement-II: Friendly aliens are the subjects of those countries that have cordial relations with India.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: enemy aliens enjoy lesser rights than friendly aliens, for example they lack protection against arrest and detention (Article 22). Statement-II is correct: friendly aliens are the subjects of countries with cordial relations with India. The definition of friendly aliens does not explain why enemy aliens have fewer rights.
w: Statement-II only defines friendly aliens; it gives no reason why enemy aliens enjoy fewer rights.
Statement-II is correct: it defines friendly aliens that way.
Statement-I is correct: enemy aliens enjoy lesser rights, for example no Article 22 protection.

questions.q:
Match the persons in List-I with the description in List-II.

List-I
A. Friendly alien
B. Enemy alien
C. Citizen
D. Naturalised citizen of India

List-II
1. Subject of a country at war with India
2. Subject of a country with cordial relations with India
3. Full member of the State who owes allegiance and enjoys all civil and political rights
4. Eligible for the office of President of India, unlike a naturalised citizen in the USA
questions.e: Friendly aliens - cordial relations; enemy aliens - at war; citizens - full members with allegiance; naturalised citizens can be President in India.
w: Interchanges B and C: Enemy alien belongs with 'Subject of a country at war with India' and Citizen with 'Full member of the State who owes allegiance and enjoys all civil and political rights'.

Interchanges C and D: Citizen belongs with 'Full member of the State who owes allegiance and enjoys all civil and political rights' and Naturalised citizen of India with 'Eligible for the office of President of India, unlike a naturalised citizen in the USA'.

Interchanges B and D: Enemy alien belongs with 'Subject of a country at war with India' and Naturalised citizen of India with 'Eligible for the office of President of India, unlike a naturalised citizen in the USA'.

questions.q: In which one of the following federal systems is each person a citizen both of the nation and of the particular state to which he or she belongs?
o: None of the federal systems, since federalism requires a single citizenship
questions.e: In the USA a person is a citizen of the USA and of the state in which he resides, giving double citizenship. Canada and India have single citizenship.
w: India provides for only single citizenship.
Canada, like India, has single citizenship.
The USA is the standard example of double citizenship.

questions.q: Under which of the following Articles can Parliament prescribe residence within a state or union territory as a condition for certain employments or appointments in that state or union territory?
questions.e: Exception 1 - Parliament (under Article 16) can prescribe residence as a condition for certain employments.
w: Article 15 bars discrimination on specified grounds and does not provide for residence requirements in employment.
Article 19 allows restrictions on residence in tribal areas to protect Scheduled Tribes, not residence requirements for employment.
Article 35-A concerned the permanent residents of the erstwhile Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.q: The freedom of movement and residence under Article 19 is restricted in tribal areas mainly in order to
questions.a: protect the culture, language and customs of Scheduled Tribes and their traditional vocation and property
o: protect the culture, language and customs of Scheduled Tribes and their traditional vocation and property
reserve government employment in the tribal areas for the residents of the state concerned
let the state legislature define its permanent residents and confer special rights on them
prevent the citizens of tribal areas from migrating to other states in search of work
questions.e: Outsiders' right to enter, reside and settle in tribal areas is restricted to protect scheduled tribes' culture, language, customs, vocation and property.
w: That is the purpose of the residence requirement under Article 16, not of the tribal-area restriction.
That was the Article 35-A arrangement of erstwhile Jammu and Kashmir.
The restriction limits the entry and settlement of outsiders, not the movement of tribals.

questions.q: Until 2019 the legislature of the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir could define its permanent residents. This power was based on
questions.a: Article 35-A, inserted by the 1954 Order issued by the President under Article 370
o: Article 35-A, inserted by the 1954 Order issued by the President under Article 370
Article 35-A, inserted by a constitutional amendment of Parliament in 1954 under Article 368
Article 370 itself, as originally enacted, which listed all the rights of permanent residents
the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957
questions.e: Article 35-A was inserted by the 1954 Order issued by the President under Article 370; the 2019 Order superseded it.
w: It came by a presidential order under Article 370, not by an amendment of Parliament under Article 368.
Article 35-A was inserted later by the 1954 Order; Article 370 as enacted did not list these rights.
The 1957 Act related to residential qualification for non-Gazetted posts in certain other states.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the problem created by double citizenship that is avoided by single citizenship in India?
questions.a: A state may discriminate in favour of its own citizens in voting, public office and professions
o: A state may discriminate in favour of its own citizens in voting, public office and professions
Citizens cannot owe allegiance to the national government at all
The Union cannot make any laws that apply to the citizens of every state
Citizens lose the right to move freely from one state to another
questions.e: Double citizenship lets states discriminate in favour of their own citizens in voting, public offices and professions.
w: Double citizenship, as in the USA, means a person owes allegiance to both the nation and the state, so this option states the opposite.
Double citizenship does not by itself limit the Union's power to legislate for all citizens.
Free movement is not the problem identified; discrimination by states is.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Constitution of Canada, like that of India, has introduced the system of single citizenship.
2. In the USA a person is a citizen of the USA, and the states have no citizenship of their own.
3. Although the Indian Constitution is federal and envisages a dual polity, it provides for only a single citizenship.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: a US person is a citizen of the USA and of the particular state, owing allegiance to both. Statement 3 is correct. So only 1 and 3 are correct.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect:
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
With reference to the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957, consider the following statements:

1. Parliament enacted it on the strength of the power under Article 16 to prescribe residence as a condition for certain employments.
2. The Act authorised the Government of India to prescribe a residential qualification for Gazetted posts in certain states.
3. The Act applied to Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur and Tripura.
4. No state other than Andhra Pradesh and Telangana now has such a provision.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Parliament enacted the 1957 Act under Article 16, which lets it prescribe residence as a condition for certain employments. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Act related to non-Gazetted posts, not Gazetted posts. Statement 3 is correct: the Act applied to Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur and Tripura. Statement 4 is correct: at present no state other than Andhra Pradesh and Telangana has such a provision, which survives under Article 371-D. So only 1, 3 and 4 are correct.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: only Andhra Pradesh and Telangana now have such a provision, under Article 371-D.
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: Article 16(3) empowers Parliament to prescribe residence for certain employments.
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: Article 16(3) empowers Parliament to prescribe residence for certain employments.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the equal treatment of citizens in India:

1. Citizens enjoy the same civil and political rights all over the country irrespective of the state in which they are born or reside, subject to some exceptions.
2. A state may offer concessions in education fees to its residents without violating Article 15.
3. The freedom of movement and residence under Article 19 is subject to the protection of the interests of any scheduled tribe.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct: Article 15 does not bar discrimination on the ground of residence. Statement 3 is correct. So only 1, 2 and 3 are correct.
w: '2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir:

1. Article 35-A was inserted by a Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order issued by the President under Article 368.
2. Till 2019 its legislature could confer special rights on permanent residents regarding employment under the state government, acquisition of immovable property, settlement and scholarships.
3. The Order of 2019 supplemented the earlier 1954 Order, which remained in force.
4. The special status was abolished by the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 itself.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the 1954 Order was issued under Article 370. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 2019 Order superseded the 1954 Order. Statement 4 is incorrect: it was abolished by a new presidential order of 2019; the Reorganisation Act bifurcated the state into two Union territoriesfn 3). So only 2 is correct.
w: '4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding exceptions to the absence of discrimination among citizens:

1. The power to prescribe residence as a condition of public employment is found in Article 15.
2. Parliament's power under Article 16 covers employment under a local authority within the state or union territory.
3. Parliament's power under Article 16 to prescribe residence relates to posts under the Central Government and not to those under a state or a local authority.
4. Parliament, and not a state legislature, can prescribe residence within a state as a condition for certain employment under that state.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it is Article 16; Article 15 does not cover residence. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the power covers employments under a state or union territory and local or other authorities within it. Statement 4 is correct: the power under Article 16 belongs to Parliament. So only 2 and 4 are correct.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. In a system of double citizenship, a person enjoys a single set of rights conferred by the national government.
2. Under double citizenship a state may discriminate in favour of its own citizens in the right to vote.
3. In India, citizens owe allegiance to the Union as well as to their state of residence.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: dual sets of rights, one national and one from the state. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: allegiance only to the Union. So only 2 is correct.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. India has witnessed communal riots, class conflicts, caste wars, linguistic clashes and ethnic disputes despite the single citizenship system.
2. Single citizenship and uniform rights were meant to promote fraternity and unity among the people of India.
3. The goal of building a united and integrated Indian nation has been fully realised.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: despite single citizenship, India has seen communal riots, class conflicts, caste wars, linguistic clashes and ethnic disputes. Statement 2 is correct: single citizenship and uniform rights were meant to promote fraternity and unity. Statement 3 is incorrect: such conflicts show that the goal of a united and integrated nation has not been fully realised. So only 1 and 2 are correct.

concepts.name: Constitutional provisions: who became citizens on 26 January 1950

questions.q: A person domiciled in India became a citizen of India at the commencement of the Constitution if he or she fulfilled which one of the following sets of conditions?
questions.a: Born in India, or either parent born in India, or ordinarily resident in India for five years immediately before the commencement
o: Born in India, or either parent born in India, or ordinarily resident in India for five years immediately before the commencement
Born in India, and both parents born in India, and ordinarily resident in India for five years
Born in India, or either grandparent born in undivided India, or ordinarily resident in India for ten years
Either parent a citizen of India, or ordinarily resident in India for five years, but not born in India
questions.e: Domicile plus any one of three conditions - born in India; either parent born in India; ordinarily resident five years immediately before commencement.
w: Article 5 requires any one of the three conditions, not all of them, and one parent suffices.
Grandparent birth and ten years' residence are not conditions under Article 5, which speaks of birth, parent's birth and five years' residence.
Birth in India is itself one of the alternative conditions, so excluding it is wrong.

questions.q: Rahim migrated from Pakistan to India on 1 September 1948, and his father had been born in undivided India. Under the Constitution he became an Indian citizen only if
questions.a: he was registered as a citizen after being resident in India for six months before his application
o: he was registered as a citizen after being resident in India for six months before his application
he had been ordinarily resident in India since the date of his migration
he had been ordinarily resident in India for five years before 26 January 1950
he was registered by an Indian consular representative in Pakistan
questions.e: Those migrating on or after 19 July 1948 had to be registered, and registration needed six months' residence before the application.
w: That test applies to migrants who came before 19 July 1948, and Rahim came after it.
Five years' residence is a condition for persons domiciled in India, not for migrants.
Registration by a consular representative is the route for persons of Indian origin residing outside India.

questions.q: Meera went to Pakistan from India in April 1947 and returned to India in 1949 to settle. Under the Constitution she could become a citizen of India if
questions.a: she was resident in India for six months before applying for registration
o: she was resident in India for six months before applying for registration
she had been ordinarily resident in India since the date of her return, without any registration
she was resident in India for twelve months before applying for registration
she had migrated to Pakistan before 1 March 1947
questions.e: Persons who migrated to Pakistan after 1 March 1947 and returned for resettlement needed six months' residence before applying for registration.
w: A returnee has to be registered after the residence; ordinary residence alone does not make her a citizen.
The residence required before applying for registration is six months, not twelve.
This contradicts the facts: she left in April 1947, after 1 March 1947, which is the date the provision turns on.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the constitutional provision on a person who has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of a foreign state?
questions.a: He or she shall not be a citizen of India nor be deemed to be one
o: He or she shall not be a citizen of India nor be deemed to be one
He or she continues as a citizen of India but loses the right to vote
He or she ceases to be a citizen only after an order of the Central Government
He or she shall be registered as an overseas citizen of India
questions.e: No person shall be a citizen of India or deemed to be one if he or she has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of a foreign state.
w: Under Article 9 such a person is not a citizen at all, not merely a citizen without the vote.
Article 9 operates without any order of the Central Government.
Overseas citizenship is a later statutory scheme and not a constitutional consequence.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the rights of citizenship of certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India?
questions.e: Article 8 deals with the rights of citizenship of certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India.
w: Article 6 deals with certain persons who migrated to India from Pakistan.
Article 7 deals with certain migrants to Pakistan.
Article 10 deals with continuance of the rights of citizenship.

w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: Article 10 provides continuance subject to Parliament's law.
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: Article 10 provides continuance subject to Parliament's law.

Statement 3 is incorrect: the date is after 1 March 1947, not 1 March 1948. Statement 4 is incorrect: those who migrated to Pakistan after 26 January 1950 and returned are decided under the 1955 Act. o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I

o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect

questions.e: A person who migrated to Pakistan after 1 March 1947 and returned for resettlement must have resided in India for six months before applying for registration (A-2). concepts.name: Other constitutional provisions and the Citizenship Act 1955

the identification of the persons who became citizens of India on 26 January 1950 and of their descendants
the acquisition of citizenship only, leaving loss of citizenship to the Constitution
the citizenship of persons domiciled in India at the commencement of the Constitution

citizenship acquired under the Act, and not that acquired earlier under the Constitution at its commencement

questions.q:
Match the benefit or condition in List-I with the example in List-II for OCI Cardholders.

List-I
A. Special permission or permit required
B. Parity with Non-Resident Indians
C. Parity with Indian nationals
D. Exemption from registration with the FRRO or FRO

List-II
1. Inter-country adoption of Indian children
2. Domestic air fares and entry fees to monuments and museums
3. Any length of stay
4. Mountaineering or journalistic activities
questions.e: Mountaineering or journalistic activities need special permission or a permit (A-4). Inter-country adoption of Indian children is at par with Non-Resident Indians (B-1). Domestic air fares and entry fees to monuments and museums are at par with Indian nationals (C-2). An OCI Cardholder is exempt from registration with the FRRO or FRO for any length of stay (D-3).
w: Interchanges A and C: Special permission or permit required belongs with 'Mountaineering or journalistic activities' and Parity with Indian nationals with 'Domestic air fares and entry fees to monuments and museums'.

Interchanges C and D: Parity with Indian nationals belongs with 'Domestic air fares and entry fees to monuments and museums' and Exemption from registration with the FRRO or FRO with 'Any length of stay'.
Interchanges B and D: Parity with Non-Resident Indians belongs with 'Inter-country adoption of Indian children' and Exemption from registration with the FRRO or FRO with 'Any length of stay'.
